global: The ridge is ours and the dead lie where they fell. A hard day's work, and the ancestors may judge it kindly.
Some stood with us at the ford today, and some merely watched from the hill. Both will be remembered in their proper measure.
{troop_count} men marched out and {troop_count} marched home. The arithmetic of honour is not always a comfortable sum.
{enemy_faction} will tell its own tale of this field, and it will be a shorter one than they wish. Let the matter rest.
Victory on the causeway, won by stubbornness more than skill. I shall take it, and I shall not pretend otherwise.
A grey dawn, a bloody noon, and a victory no minstrel will bother to rhyme. Glory is rarely as loud as it is promised.
The standard of our house was nearly torn from its pole today. It did not fall, and neither did the men beneath it.
Whatever is said of this battle in the taverns, know that the fighting was honest and the victory was hard-won.
whisper: Ser {player}, you fought well at my flank today. I do not yet know what that means for us, but I will not forget it.
The field was won together, which changes nothing between us beyond one afternoon. Keep your distance, and we shall get on.
You held the line beside us. Do not mistake one shared victory for a shared oath, friend.
Your blade was useful today, ser {player}. Whether your counsel is equally sound remains to be seen.
We won the field, and I shall grant you your share of the credit. Beyond that, we keep to our own roads.
Ser {player}, I noticed where you stood when the charge broke. A good eye. I would like to know whose eye it was.
An alliance of one afternoon is still an alliance, but I will not write it into any charter yet.
Thank you for the flank, ser {player}. I would rather owe you nothing, yet I find I owe you something.
face: Stay your horse, traveller. We fought on the same field today, so I will not raise my shield to you. Pass, and mind the mud on the road.
Ser {player}, the ground still smells of battle. We won, and I suppose that buys you a greeting. State your business briefly.
You are the one who held the eastern bank. I saw it. Go your way in peace, and do not expect me to sing your praises at the fire.
Well met on this sorry road. Our banners stood together today, which is more than I expected of anyone. Keep the peace and we shall see.
Ser {player}, the victory is ours and I am tired. Go with the blessing of whatever ancestors you keep, and do not linger.
We may have bled on the same ground, traveller, but that is not the same as sharing a hearth. Good day to you.
A fine fight, ser {player}, though the price was steep. I shall remember who stood firm, and I shall remember who did not.
Hail, traveller. Our swords sang together this morning. I will be watching which way your banner turns when the next war comes.

global: Ser {player} held the eastern bank when all others faltered. Let it be known that this knight's courage shall be sung in our hall.
Hail to the brave ser {player} and the folk who stood with them! Today the ridge belongs to honest blades, and I am proud to say so.
Our victory was born of a comrade's steady hand. Ser {player}, I drink to you, and I hope the ancestors see fit to repeat the favour.
The field is won and the wine is poured. Raise a cup to ser {player}, whose stubbornness saved more than one life today.
Three cheers for {troop_count} brave souls who never once looked back. Ser {player} led them, and I will stand as witness.
Let no one say the banners of this host fell lightly. We won this morning with ser {player} at our side, and that is a fine thing.
A bloody day, and a glorious one. Ser {player}, your name will be spoken at the feast of this fief for years to come.
Honour to ser {player}, who fought as a true knight fights. May our oaths hold as firmly as your shield did today.
whisper: Ser {player}, you stood where the line was thinnest and did not give a single step. I am in your debt, and I say so plainly.
That charge would have ended me without you. My sword and my house are yours to call upon, friend, whenever you will it.
We won the day together, ser {player}. Let us keep faith with it, and meet again at the next mustering if the roads allow.
I shall not forget the way you turned the flank. When the bards ask who saved my banner, I shall give them your name first.
Ser {player}, a fine morning's work. Come and share a cup at my camp tonight, and we shall talk of oaths over the fire.
You fought with such honour that I felt shamed for every hesitant stroke of my own. Thank you, ser {player}. Truly.
Your courage today will be the tale I tell my children, friend. May the ancestors grant us both a quieter war next season.
Should {enemy_faction} ever bring their banners to your door, know that mine shall ride beside yours, ser {player}. This I swear.
face: Ser {player}! Our swords sang as one today, and I would be a poor knight if I did not greet you with open arms. Well met, friend.
Pause a moment, friend. I wished to say that the victory was yours as much as mine. Ride on with the ancestors' favour, ser {player}.
There you are, ser {player}. I was hoping our paths would cross after that slaughter. You are a sight for weary eyes, traveller.
The road is quiet now, thanks to you. Walk with me a little, ser {player}, and tell me how you came to hold that bank so well.
Ser {player}, your banner was the last thing I saw before the smoke rolled in, and I was glad of it. May your shadow never grow shorter.
Any ford you cross beside me is a ford we shall win, ser {player}. I have sworn it on my ancestors, and I mean every word.
A proud day for our company, and a prouder one for you. Ser {player}, I greet you as a brother-in-arms and will not hear otherwise.
Friend, the field is yours and the road is open. Ride on, and if {enemy_faction} stops you, send word and I shall ride for you.
